title: Elul: letters of apology
hook: many write or call to apologize before the High Holy Days
tomorrow: a fish head on a holiday table? there's a wish inside it.

segments.voice: Yesterday, Elul: a month of getting ready, a little prayer, a little honesty, a little giving, a runway and not a deadline. Thirty days of getting ready. Today, the hardest of the three.
screen: `THIRTY DAYS OF GETTING READY.` → `THE HARDEST OF THE THREE.`

segments.voice: Some messages sit in drafts for weeks, the ones that start, hey, about what I said. In Elul, people finally send them: letters, calls, a knock on a door. Here's why the timing matters. The Mishnah says Yom Kippur atones for a great deal, but there's one kind of wrong it can't fix on its own. Not by fasting, not by praying all day. Which one?
screen: `STILL IN DRAFTS.` → `HEY, ABOUT WHAT I SAID.` → `WHAT CAN'T THE DAY FIX?`

segments.voice: Here's the Mishnah's answer. For wrongs between a person and God, Yom Kippur atones. For wrongs between a person and another person, Yom Kippur does not atone until they make peace with the one they hurt. The day can't do your apologizing for you. That's why Elul fills with letters and calls. And the Talmud adds a story about the other side. When someone had wronged Rabbi Zeira, he would walk back and forth in front of that person, on purpose, so they'd have an easy chance to come and make it right. The hurt one makes the door easy to open. Now a neighbor who says it too. Owen's tradition keeps a saying of Jesus in Matthew: "first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift." If you remember at the altar that someone has something against you, leave the gift and go. Shared ground: make peace with the person before you come before God. And one honest difference. Matthew's saying names no season; it happens whenever the gift is brought. The Jewish calendar also gives it a season and a date: a month to prepare, and a day it has to be done before. Something to tell a friend tonight: Rabbi Zeira made himself easy to apologize to.
screen: `THE DAY ATONES BETWEEN YOU AND GOD.` · `BETWEEN PEOPLE, MAKE PEACE FIRST.` · `RABBI ZEIRA WALKS BY ON PURPOSE.` · `MATTHEW: FIRST BE RECONCILED.` · then, large: `APOLOGIZE BEFORE THE DAY.`

segments.voice: Choose one person you owe an apology. Write the first two lines by hand: name what you did, plainly, without an if or a but. You don't have to send it today; Elul gives you time to get it right.
screen: `ONE PERSON.` · `WHAT YOU DID, PLAINLY.` · `NO IF, NO BUT.`

segments.voice: Elul: the month for apologies, because Yom Kippur covers wrongs against God, and waits on wrongs against people.
Your line: apologize before the day. The day can't do it for you. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: In the weeks before Yom Kippur, Jews traditionally ask forgiveness of family, friends and coworkers, in person, by letter or by phone; some say a general request for forgiveness on the eve of Yom Kippur as well.
